## Mathematical models 

- Mathematical models help us to understand the data
- In a regression setting the model describes a function that maps input to real-valued outputs 
- Thinking back to hypotheses from last week. We can use mathematical models to validate our hypotheses/research questions 
- E.g. How does the number of bedrooms affect house price? 
- Or the relationship between time spent studying to grade 

## Machine learning 

- A specific type of mathematical model 
- A model which improves after data is taken into account. 
- The learning part is about automatically finding patterns 

::: {.notes}
In later weeks of the course we will look at machine learning concepts. 
:::

# Functions 

## What is a function?
It is a mathematical opertaion which maps an input value to an output value. 

## Mathematical description of a function 

- f(x)=y
- Maps values from a domain () to a range (). 
- In the applied sciences the domain and range typically R,Z,N
- Natural numbers 0,1,2,3,4,5,6…
- Integers … -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, … 
- Real numbers 

## Data represented algebraically 

- This is the data represented algebraically. 
- Algebra – expressing a generalised, or abstract, form
- Typically a vector of numbers X^n

## Examples of functions 
Probability density function 

# Linear equations 

## A linear combination of variables 
A specific combination of variables 

## Linear equation(s)

- A system of multiple linear functions 
- Can be represented by matrices 
- Systems of linear equatiosn can have 0, 1 or many solutions 

## Example 1 

```{=tex}
\begin{align}
x+y=10
\end{align}
```

. . .

::: {.incremental}
- What could x and y be? 
- Could have x=y=5
- Or x=2.5 and y=7.5
:::

. . .

There are many solutions!!!
Many solutions = under-specified

::: {.notes}
Under-specified but simple to solve!
:::

## Example 2 

```{=tex}
\begin{align}
x+y=10
\\
2x+y=15
\end{align}
```
. . .

::: {.incremental}
- In school might have solved this using substitution. 
- Rearrange the first equation to get y=10-x
- Substituting in we get 2x+(10-x)=15
- x+10=15  > x=5 > y=5
:::

. . .

There is exactly one solution

::: {.notes}
Perfectly specified and we can solve it without too much difficulty 
:::

## Example 3 

```{=tex}
\begin{align}
x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=10
\\ x_1+4x_2+x_3+x_4=25
\\ x_1+4x_2+43x_3+x_4=37
\\ x_1+4x_2+7x_3+59x_4=1073
\end{align}
```

. . .

Very hard to solve!

::: {.notes}
An example (when things get more complicated)
